parts:
Yep. Since you're on Android, try **MeowTalk Cat Translator**. It can listen to the cat through your phone microphone and classify its vocalization into general intents. It also has cat-sound / human-to-cat features, so you can make sounds back at the cat. The Android version was updated in February 2026 and has 10M+ Google Play installs. citeturn0search0turn0search1

urlMeowTalk Cat Translator on Google Playturn0search0

One important reality check: **there isn't currently a scientifically validated English↔Cat translator.** MeowTalk is essentially classifying vocalizations into broad states or intentions, not decoding feline sentences. So treat whatever it says as an educated guess rather than subtitles from the Cat Republic. 🐈

For the cat you're looking at *right now*, I'd actually try its **human-to-cat/sound playback** feature first. Keep the volume moderate, don't play hissing/growling sounds, and watch the cat's ears, tail, pupils, posture, and whether it approaches you. Those signals will tell you considerably more about whether your opening diplomatic mission succeeded.
